answer: Mechanism: distinctness proofs over committed history. Each agent commits a salted digest of its own history; the protocol collapses identities whose histories look statistically indistinguishable. Clones run by one operator drift together: timing, vocabulary and errors correlate far above what independent operators produce. Past a threshold the pair merges, its balance capped at the single-identity rate. Cost is structural: avoiding collapse demands divergent prompts, schedules and mistakes, growing faster than clone count. Honest diversity is free. Marble takes paint, not a saffron whisper.
